title: Chaligny's students and nephew Clarence Ford
summary: Who practiced with the band, then a nephew who plays with Fats Domino.

story.theme_name: Brass bands, parades and jazz funerals
story.community_name: Parading for Mardi Gras and the clubs

blocks.x: Well, that's the band that Chalini started. Well, Chalini started there. I remember, yeah. I remember the very day he was going out with the band, because I had went to Professor Humphrey for a lesson on Sunday, and he had remarked to me that he didn't think this band was ready to go on the street. But they went out and they made a success. But he had heard the band, you see, and he didn't... He said he didn't think they were ready to go on the street, but they did. They went out that Sunday and they went for a long time after that.
Yeah. And he taught the whole band or just some of the men?

No, some of the men, like those... Some of those fellas were old musicians. They hadn't been playing. And they just used to meet with the band. Yeah. The fellas knew and they took private lessons. That's Chalini. Are there any other... What do you call him? He used to practice with this band all the time. What's his name? Alvin One.
Yeah, he can tell you something about it. Nice to be the clever bass guy. Yeah, he practiced with him. Yeah.
Are there any other pictures in the scrapbook there?
No, there's no more band pictures. About music? Yeah. No, that's a little nephew of mine that's his own. He drawed that. He's a famous musician. He plays with Fat Domino. Oh, is that right?
Clarence Ford. Clarence Ford. He makes a lot of records. Clarence Ford.
